Reigniting the Verdant Era Chapter 113: Why Does Your Voice Sound a Little Breathless?

Monday, 9:00 AM sharp.

Inside the meeting room of Huayue Film and Television.

Ying Zhicheng was chairing the meeting. After listening to the entire project proposal and confirming there was nothing to add, he looked toward Yuan Wanqing on his left.

"The new album will go live today at 12 PM sharp, and we've already been warming it up for a month," Ying Zhicheng said. "In a moment, it will start trending on Weibo. Your studio needs to coordinate well. Use your official account to post a Weibo update; the content and style should follow the proposal."

"You'll start running promotional events in the afternoon. The entire schedule has been arranged."

"There will be exclusive interviews with three entertainment media outlets, some simple interactions with a few major entertainment influencers on Weibo, and several variety shows to follow."

"Especially on the variety shows, the script will arrange for you to have a singing performance segment. You need to seize that opportunity."

"Many people will question whether your skills are still there after being retired from the industry for over a decade."

"So, the three variety shows are all targeted. One is for entertainment, where you'll sing a few climactic snippets; another is a temporary guest spot on a celebrity travel show, where you're required to sing a cappella to highlight authenticity; the last one is a singing competition show to showcase your complete vocal ability."

The resources of Huayue Film and Television were quite abundant within Qianjiang Province.

They also placed sufficient importance on Yuan Wanqing's comeback.

After hearing Ying Zhicheng's words, Yuan Wanqing nodded with a calm expression, indicating that she understood. After the meeting, she left the company with her assistant, got into a minivan, and went to prepare for the afternoon's events.

Soon, as various promotional materials and Weibo trends began to ferment, more and more news about Yuan Wanqing's new album emerged.

The new album, "A Decade Like a Dream," quickly entered the public eye.

Faced with this singer who had been poised to achieve diva status at the start of the century, many from the older generation sighed with emotion, never expecting to see the day she would make a comeback.

But there was no shortage of doubt and belittling remarks, picking faults with the new album.

In the first few days after the album's release, the hype was indeed quite good.

Yuan Wanqing's title track also caused a stir online for a while.

But as other new things emerged on the internet, the public's focus quickly shifted.

This was already a period when physical album sales had hit rock bottom, so Huayue Film and Television was mainly focusing on promoting the online digital album.

But despite pouring in a large amount of resources, the digital album sales on various platforms were just a drop in the bucket.

On album charts like QQ Music's, it barely broke into the top ten before falling off a few days later.

And of the ten songs on the new album, only the title track "Dancing Like a Dream" briefly made it into the top three before its popularity faded and it dropped out of the top ten.

If these results belonged to a newcomer in the music industry, it wouldn't be considered a complete failure, and might even be seen as pretty good.

But for Yuan Wanqing, it was indeed far below expectations.

As for the matter of Yuan Wanqing's comeback, it was almost completely irrelevant to the high school students far away at Fu First High.

Most of them were just babies born at the end of the last century and were not at all familiar with Yuan Wanqing, let alone interested in paying attention to such entertainment gossip.

Only someone like Li Luo, because of his connection to Yan Zhusheng, had a slight understanding of the situation.

After the new album's results had basically settled, Li Luo also let out a sigh.

In his past life, he hadn't heard much about Yuan Wanqing's comeback, which meant this new album truly hadn't made much of a splash.

Besides, the entertainment industry changes rapidly. Once you miss an opportunity, you might never get another chance to become popular again.

One could actually draw a conclusion from Yan Zhusheng herself: Yuan Wanqing's own singing ability was definitely not bad, and could even be described as very strong.

But as the internet gradually entered the smartphone era, the importance of traffic had begun to overshadow talent itself.

Many talented people merely needed a single opportunity, a catalyst to leverage traffic.

And clearly, Yuan Wanqing had failed to do that.

After checking Yuan Wanqing's current situation on the computer, Li Luo became a little more careful when he spoke to Yan Zhusheng in the classroom during the day.

But Yan Zhusheng quickly noticed his strangeness and couldn't help but ask, "What are you worried about?"

"Nothing," Li Luo shook his head, then said, "Your mom's new album is out. Have you downloaded it on your phone? We can listen together at noon."

"Oh," Yan Zhusheng nodded. "Did you listen to it?"

"I listened to it a bit these past two days when I got home."

"Is it good?"

"Besides the title track, I quite like 'Roaming in a Dream' and 'First Heart'. They really suit your mother's singing style."

"I'm glad you like it." Yan Zhusheng didn't care about the album's performance. After hearing Li Luo's praise, she earnestly took note of it in her heart.

During the noon break, she secretly passed one earbud over to him, then lay down on her desk, sleeping with her face turned toward Li Luo.

Listening to Yuan Wanqing's singing, with the singer's daughter sleeping beside him, Li Luo rested on his desk and looked at Yan Zhusheng, feeling that this was all a bit strange.

However, halfway through the lunch break, a message suddenly popped up on Yan Zhusheng's phone.

She stole a glance at it, then told Li Luo she was going to the restroom and ran out to take a call.

When she came back, since the lunch break wasn't over yet, the rest of the class was still resting.

So Yan Zhusheng took a scratch paper notebook from Li Luo's desk and wrote in it.

Yan Zhusheng: My mom called me.

Yan Zhusheng: She said she should be free to come to the parent-teacher conference on Saturday.

Li Luo glanced at the words on the scratch paper, one eyebrow raising as some guesses formed in his mind.

Could it be that because of the new album's poor performance, her originally packed schedule had been reduced?

Looking at it this way, it wasn't entirely a bad thing. At least she could attend her daughter's first high school parent-teacher conference.

Li Luo: Then is your mom free at noon on Saturday?

Yan Zhusheng: I don't know either. Why?

Li Luo: Didn't Senior Sister say before that her mom wanted to treat us and our parents to a meal?

Yan Zhusheng: Oh, that. I'll ask her again tonight then.

When evening came.

There were about ten minutes left in the second evening self-study session.

Li Luo pretended to go to the restroom, but in reality, he went downstairs toward the sports field.

A short while later, Yan Zhusheng followed him out, and they met up on the field.

Originally, he and Yan Zhusheng had agreed to go for a run on the field after the second evening self-study session to get some exercise.

But Yan Zhusheng later thought it over and said that if Ying Chanxi and Xu Youyu had to wait for Li Luo to go home together, it would be too much trouble for them.

And so, this current suggestion was made.

Li Luo was the class president, so no one would say anything if he disappeared for ten minutes or so during the second session.

Yan Zhusheng skillfully put an earbud in Li Luo's ear, then put one in her own, turned on the music on her phone, and the two began to run laps.

The first few times they went night running, Li Luo was still a little unaccustomed to it.

But as the number of times increased, and with Yan Zhusheng by his side, Li Luo gradually began to enjoy the rhythm of his body.

He had to admit, having a young body was great.

In his past life, by the time he was 35, his body was already a complete mess.

Pimples, oily face, heavy dark circles, thinning hair, a pudgy physique, and poor kidney function. He was lethargic every day, with no energy for anything.

Just walking up the stairs or carrying a delivery package could leave him breathless, let alone running a few steps.

Now, living a second life and after starting to night run with Yan Zhusheng, Li Luo suddenly realized he needed to consciously keep exercising.

Just playing basketball occasionally wasn't enough.

Doing something like this, running every day, would be quite good if he stuck with it.

To be honest, Li Luo used to find the daily running exercises arranged by the school a bit annoying.

But only after he got older did he realize that forced activities like that, exercising for just ten-odd minutes a day, were enough to keep a person's body relatively healthy and energetic.

It was just that after entering the workforce, most people couldn't even manage ten-plus minutes of exercise a day.

After all, from dawn till dusk they were being squeezed dry by their bosses. Their energy and spirit were long gone, so where would they find the strength to work out?

As he ran, Li Luo let his thoughts drift, thinking about these things.

It wasn't until Yan Zhusheng suddenly stopped that Li Luo also stopped, asking in confusion, "Why did you stop? Class isn't over yet, right?"

"We have time right now, so I can give my mom a call," Yan Zhusheng said. "Didn't you say I should ask about lunch on Saturday?"

"Now?" Li Luo paused for a moment, then nodded. "Sure, go ahead and ask."

So, Yan Zhusheng dialed Yuan Wanqing's number.

Within a few seconds, the call connected.

"Hello?" Yuan Wanqing's confused voice came from the other end. "Shengsheng? Is something wrong?"

"Mom," Yan Zhusheng glanced at Li Luo. "After you attend the parent-teacher conference on Saturday, do you have anything else to do?"

"On Saturday?" Yuan Wanqing asked her assistant, then said, "Nothing particularly special, I just have to go back to the company for a meeting in the afternoon. What's up?"

"Oh, it's like this," Yan Zhusheng explained. "A friend's parent would like to invite you to have a meal together then."

"Is that so?" Yuan Wanqing furrowed her brow, feeling it was a bit troublesome.

Although she was considered past her prime now, she was still a public figure and didn't really want to get involved with parents from the school.

But the thought that it was Yan Zhusheng's friend made Yuan Wanqing's tone soften. "Which friend is it? Does Mom know them?"

"It's Li Luo, the one I told you about last time," Yan Zhusheng said in a small voice. "My best friend in high school."

On the other end of the line, Yuan Wanqing fell silent.

After a few seconds of thought, she said, "Tell Li Luo that I'll be there. And thank him for me in advance."

"Okay." Yan Zhusheng glanced at Li Luo, who was standing lookout for her, and nodded gently.

Then, just as she was about to hang up, Yuan Wanqing suddenly asked again, "Shengsheng, you sound a bit out of breath. Did you catch a cold?"

"Oh... no." Yan Zhusheng shook her head and answered honestly, "Li Luo and I were just night running on the sports field, so I'm a little breathless."

"Is... is that so..." Yuan Wanqing's tone became a bit solemn. "Well... keeping up with exercise is a good thing. I have something to take care of here, so I'll hang up now. See you on Saturday."

"Okay, bye-bye."

After hanging up, Yan Zhusheng walked over to Li Luo with a rather cheerful gait and lightly patted his shoulder. "My mom agreed. She'll come to eat with us then."

(End of Chapter)
